title: Quiz: Scaling, Encoding, and the recipes Pipeline

questions.text: You are running k-means clustering on age (range 18–85) and income (range $1,000–$500,000) without scaling. What will happen?
options: k-means will balance both variables equally
Income will dominate cluster assignments because it has a much larger range
Age will dominate because it is an integer
k-means is unaffected by variable scale
questions.explanation: k-means uses Euclidean distance. A difference of 1 year in age is trivial compared to a difference of $10,000 in income. Without scaling, income completely dominates the distance calculation and age has essentially no influence on clustering.

questions.text: Which scaling method is most appropriate when a variable has not been winsorised and still contains extreme outliers?
options: No scaling is needed for outlier-containing variables
questions.explanation: Robust scaling uses the median and IQR rather than the mean and SD, making it resistant to outliers. Z-score and Min-Max are both pulled toward extreme values.

questions.text: Why should plan_tier (Bronze < Silver < Gold < Platinum) use ordinal encoding rather than one-hot encoding?
options: Because it has more than 2 levels
Because it is ordered — encoding as integers 1-4 preserves the natural rank
Because one-hot encoding always causes data leakage
Because Bronze is the reference category
questions.explanation: plan_tier is an ordinal variable with a natural ordering. Encoding as integers 1 (Bronze) to 4 (Platinum) preserves that ordering. One-hot encoding would treat all tiers as unordered, discarding meaningful information.

questions.text: In a recipes pipeline, step_normalize() should come before step_impute_median() to avoid computing means on missing-value-containing columns.
questions.explanation: step_impute_median() must come BEFORE step_normalize(). Normalization computes means and SDs from the data; if missing values are still present, the statistics will be based on incomplete data. Impute first, then scale.

questions.text: What is data leakage in the context of a preprocessing pipeline?
options: When data is accidentally deleted during cleaning
When information from the test set influences the training-phase parameters (e.g. imputation values)
When the model is deployed to production without testing
When a variable has near-zero variance
questions.explanation: Data leakage occurs when test-set information influences how the training pipeline is built — e.g. computing the median across train+test before imputing. This gives the model illegitimate access to information it would not have in production, inflating measured performance.
